[[section:Step 5: Make strong or weak acid]]
- Drag the hydrogen chloride canister onto a container with water to dissolve it into acid
- It dissolves until acid is 40% of the liquid (500 mL of water takes at most 333 mL of acid); the rest of the gas stays in the canister
- For weaker acid, measure out the strong acid with a Dropper or Graduated Cylinder and add water
[[gap:4]]
[[text:Note: hydrogen chloride poured into a container with base is used up neutralizing the base|color=#853737|align=center]]

[[section:Step 6: Recover the base]]
[[image:vanilla_chem_ext:evaporator_b|w=24|h=24|gap=6|float=left]]
- Take the brine container from step 2, after electrolysis
- (Optional) Filter out the clay, mineral and other physical contaminants with a Water Filter
- Put the container in the Evaporator
- Make sure the Evaporator has an Energy Cell for power
- Wait until the next day for the Evaporator to finish

Fermenter manual
How to run an Acremonium fermenter.

1. Feed: put any food in the dispenser; it only counts calories.
2. Inoculate: one strain in the strain slot. It is used up at the end of the batch.
3. Harvest: at standard traits, four strains at the end of the second night. Higher growth speed shortens the batch; higher yield means more strains.
4. Modules: efficiency, performance and quality all do the same thing here, taking power off the draw, down to zero.
5. Note: a harvested strain has mutated away from its parent, and over time mostly for the worse. Keep your stock in a dewar.
Strain breeding notes

[[section:Genome and resistance]]
[[image:vanilla_chem_ext:icon_antibiotic|w=24|h=24|gap=6|float=left]]
- Every strain carries a 12-letter genome. It decides resistance and nothing else - not yield, not quality
- Antibiotics you sell are booked against their own genome; the higher the cumulative sales, the likelier resistance becomes
- Once it sets in, tablets of that genome fetch far less, and customers say the drug hasn't been working lately
- Four letters of difference or more and a genome is untouched; fewer and it takes a share of the penalty
- Stop selling for a while and the cumulative figure falls away on its own, taking the resistance with it
[[gap:4]]
[[text:Tip: rotating a few sufficiently different genomes beats pushing one of them|color=#3D823F|align=center]]

[[section:Keeping stock]]
[[image:vanilla_chem_ext:icon_strain_frozen|w=24|h=24|gap=6|float=left]]
- A strain left overnight in a fridge's freezer zone becomes a frozen strain
- A frozen strain takes 3x3 cells, and a stock fridge's freezer zone is only 3x2: upgrade the fridge's storage at least once and clear the zone, or it will not freeze
- Double-click it for one strain, identical to the one that went in, as often as you like
- A strain taken out that way is only good for inoculating: blending it yields a little protein and nothing else
- A strain harvested from a fermenter has already mutated away from its parent, over time mostly for the worse
[[gap:4]]
[[text:Note: once you breed a good strain, freeze one before you put it to work|color=#853737|align=center]]
